_comment: What a body wears at birth. Keyed by BLUEPRINT key - the same key `core-blueprints` stores the body under, which for a card designed in the 'Create Agent Body' tab is the card's display name. Each entry is { "item": <inventoryItems key>, "component": <component type of this body> }: the garment is worn on the FIRST component instance of that type, through WearLogic (pure volume fit - the component must have the item's `wear.minVolume` of free volume), and a garment that does not fit is a warning, never a failed spawn. An item named here must exist in `core-inventory-items` AND declare `wear.minVolume`; a body named here is read at spawn only, so an entry naming a component the body does not have is simply not worn. WHEN A BLUEPRINT HAS AN OUTFIT, the default clothing of the spawn loadouts (`wear: true` in `core-world` initialSpawns and in `core-npcs` / card-profile initialItems) is NOT applied - the outfit is what this body wears, and a body does not wear the world's default shirt underneath its own coat. Every other loadout entry (coal, toolbelt, knives) is untouched. Read by `src/controllers/logic/OutfitLogic.js`; validated at boot; written by the 'Create Agent Body' Save. The seed entry below is not new behaviour: the generic droid wore the shipped t-shirt on its central body before this file existed, and still does.
